parsedVerdict.reasoning: AppointmentsController.ts is a presentation file, and everything in it fits that role. It declares two input form shapes (BookingForm and NoteForm) and one controller class. The class receives SchedulingService and VisitNotesService through its constructor. Both come from the business layer, which the presentation layer may depend on, so this is normal dependency wiring. Each method converts form input (for example, parsing a date string with new Date(form.startsAt)), passes the work to a business service, and formats the result with the presenter or a simple count. There is no domain rule, calculation or decision in the file. Supplying new Date() as the cancel time just passes the current time along; the cancellation rule itself stays in SchedulingService. Counting the notes for the response only shapes the output, so it is not a business rule. The file uses no framework or persistence types, and none of the deterministic checks raised a flag.
